source_acquisition.search_note: visual_source_inventory.csv 将 HidKim/K2Hawkes 标为标题精确匹配的候选；gh 只读检查其 README、递归树和 examples。仓库有 iclr2026_scenario.py 及两个 matplotlib example，但 example 只画 true/Ours，缺少 PDF 中 Exp/Gau/Ber/Bonnet 的 composite，也没有 table/Figure 3/LaTeX/plot asset 源，故不登记 sourceFile。SimiaoZuo/Transformer-Hawkes-Process 是 p.10 financial 数据脚注对应的外部数据仓库，标题和 README 不匹配本文。

paper_style.palette_strategy: Figure 1–2 使用固定五方法类别色加黑色 true 虚线；Figure 3 用蓝色 measured Ours 与黑色 O(U³) reference；8 张表全部采用黑白文字和规则，方法颜色不跨表复用。
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: PDF 中 Figure 1–3 的曲线、坐标、网格和文字以及全部表格均为可提取文字/矢量对象；未见承载图表数据的栅格 XObject，少量页面内嵌小图像不属于视觉对象。
paper_style.style_consistency: 正文、caption 和表格稳定使用 Nimbus Roman No9 L/Computer Modern，横线遵循 booktabs 风格。Figure 1–2 的 plot label 额外使用 ArialMT/AppleSymbols，Figure 3 混用 ArialMT、Computer Modern 和 Nimbus Monospace；图内字体与正文存在局部差异，表内结构和黑白规则保持一致。

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: Examples of the estimated triggering kernels in the mutually-exciting scenario. Dashed lines represent the true triggering kernels.

color.semantic_mapping: Ours、Gau、Ber、Exp、Bonnet 分别用红、青、洋红、绿、蓝；黑色表示 true kernel。

plot_grammar.legend_placement: upper-middle panel of the shared Figure 1–2 group

encodings.color: method: Ours, Exp, Bonnet, Ber, Gau; black dashed curve is truth
encodings.line: solid estimates versus black dashed true curve
encodings.facet: 3×3 matrix with row i and column j indexing g_ij

figures.data_and_statistics: 3-variate linear Hawkes synthetic process with nine true triggering kernels over s∈[0,5]. The paper states that sequences were generated over 10 trials, while this figure shows representative curves without trial aggregation, selection rule, error bars, or bands; Δ² and CPU are reported separately in Table 1.
figures.evidence_relation: Theorem 1 and Propositions 2–4 define the transformed-kernel estimator; Table 1 quantifies mutually-exciting Δ² and CPU; Appendix A Figure 1 checks the corresponding kernel shapes. The figure supplies qualitative shape evidence and does not measure accuracy, runtime, or component ablation.
design_strengths: A fixed 3×3 facet makes self- and cross-kernel shapes comparable at a glance.
True-kernel dashed lines and direct True g_ij labels preserve the comparison baseline even when y labels repeat sparsely.
All methods share the same axes and support window, making over- or under-shooting visible.
design_weaknesses: Five estimates overlap near zero; color is the main method identifier and is not robust to grayscale or color-vision limitations.
The caption does not state which trial or aggregation produced the displayed curves.
The shared legend is placed in the upper middle of the figure pair, so a cropped Figure 1 is less self-explanatory.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a fixed row/column facet for matrix-valued functions, a common support and scale, and a dashed truth curve with direct labels; keep a single legend for the whole grid.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2: Examples of the estimated triggering kernels in the refractory scenario. Dashed lines represent the true triggering kernels.

color.semantic_mapping: 沿用 Figure 1：Ours、Gau、Ber、Exp、Bonnet 为五种方法，黑色虚线为 true kernel。

plot_grammar.legend_placement: shared legend appears in upper-middle panel of Figure 1

encodings.color: method: Ours, Exp, Bonnet, Ber, Gau; black dashed curve is truth
encodings.line: solid estimates versus black dashed true curve
encodings.facet: 3×3 matrix with row i and column j indexing g_ij

figures.data_and_statistics: 3-variate refractory/non-linear Hawkes synthetic process with inhibitory diagonal kernels and non-inhibitory inter-actions. The paper reports 10 trials for Table 2, but Figure 2 displays representative curves with no trial identity, aggregate, uncertainty display, or outlier count.
figures.evidence_relation: The refractory experiment in §4.1.2 and Table 2 quantify inhibitory-kernel error/runtime; Figure 2 supplies the shape-level complement and exposes negative triggering kernels. The paper’s post-hoc intensity clipping limitation is discussed beside the table; the figure does not encode clipping or excluded Ber outliers.
design_strengths: The grid is structurally identical to Figure 1, so the change from excitation to inhibition is directly visible.
The symmetric approximately −1–1 y range makes negative kernels legible.
Shared method colors and truth-line convention make cross-regime reading inexpensive.
design_weaknesses: Figure 2 has no legend drawn inside its own crop; method colors depend on Figure 1.
Near-zero curves overlap heavily, with no marker or secondary line encoding for methods.
The caption omits the clipping condition, representative-trial rule, and Ber outlier treatment.
figures.reusable_pattern: Keep facet geometry, color mapping, truth line, and axes fixed across regimes; change only the data-generating mechanism and visible y range for a clean qualitative comparison.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3: Scaling curve of the training time regarding the dimensionality. The blue line represents the training time of Ours with respect to the dimensionality U. The black line represents a reference curve of O(U³).

color.semantic_mapping: 蓝色曲线和圆 marker 是 Ours measured training time；黑色线是 O(U³) reference。

encodings.color: blue Ours measured curve; black O(U³) reference
encodings.shape: circle markers on six measured observations
encodings.line: solid blue measured line and solid black reference line
encodings.text: axis labels and caption provide the line key

figures.data_and_statistics: Synthetic setting μ_i=0.1, g_ij(·)=0, T=100 with U∈{10,50,100,200,300,500}. The measured means are 0.68, 5.05, 26.9, 160, 478, and 2010 seconds; Table 7 supplies 5-trial standard errors, while the figure plots means only.
figures.evidence_relation: The §2.4 cubic complexity claim leads to Appendix H.2 Table 6 (U=3/15 all-method snapshot), Table 7 (Ours means and SE), and Figure 3 (log–log visual summary). It supports a practical efficiency boundary and reference comparison, without fitting or displaying a baseline scaling curve.
design_strengths: Log–log axes cover several orders of magnitude and make the theoretical reference direction legible.
Six blue markers correspond one-to-one with Table 7’s U grid.
The reference line connects a formal complexity discussion to an immediately inspectable runtime shape.
design_weaknesses: No error bars are drawn, so run variation requires cross-reading Table 7.
The reference line’s normalization and fitting interval are unspecified.
Only Ours is plotted; no baseline scaling line shares the panel, and the lack of a legend raises standalone reading cost.
figures.reusable_pattern: Pair a log–log measured-point curve with a theoretical reference line, and keep exact means and trial variation in a companion table with the same x grid.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1: Results of Exp (Bonnet et al., 2023), Gau (Xu et al., 2016), Ber (Lemonnier & Vayatis, 2014), Bonnet (Bonnet & Sangnier, 2025), and Ours on mutually-exciting scenario dataset across 10 trials with standard errors in brackets. Ñ is the average data size per trial. cpu is the CPU time in seconds. The performances not significantly (p ≥ 0.01) different from the best one under the Mann-Whitney U test (Holm, 1979) are shown in bold.

tables.uncertainty: Each T group has a mean row and a parenthesized standard-error row over 10 trials. Bold marks performances not significantly different from the best under the stated Mann–Whitney U test with Holm correction at p≥0.01.
tables.data_and_statistics: Mutually-exciting synthetic data with T=2000,3000,5000,7000 and Ñ=1318,2055,4081,5380. For Exp, Gau, Ber, Bonnet, and Ours, paired Δ² (integrated squared kernel error) and CPU seconds are reported. Accuracy and cost share the same T groups; no failure count or hardware column is shown.
tables.evidence_relation: Theorem 1/Propositions 2–4 and §2.4 complexity motivate the estimator and cost axes; Table 1 is the primary quantitative mutually-exciting comparison. Appendix A Figure 1 adds qualitative shape evidence, while Table 3 isolates support-window sensitivity.
design_strengths: Paired accuracy and CPU columns put the paper’s central quality–cost tradeoff on one decision surface.
T and Ñ expose the data-size trend, while 10-trial SE and a stated multiple-comparison rule make variation visible.
Stable method order matches Tables 2 and 4 for cross-regime reading.
design_weaknesses: Δ² is not defined in the caption, so the table depends on the body for its central metric.
Two-line mean/SE groups and 12 columns are dense at normal zoom.
CPU measurements lack hardware and implementation context, and the bold test does not show effect magnitude or comparison denominators.
tables.reusable_pattern: Arrange a quality metric and a cost metric as adjacent pairs along one experimental control axis, and place trial count, uncertainty, units, and the highlighting rule in the caption.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2: Results on refractory scenario dataset across 10 trials. Notations follow Table 1.

tables.uncertainty: Four T groups each contain a mean and parenthesized standard error over 10 trials; bold follows Table 1’s Mann–Whitney U/Holm rule. The body text states that some Ber trials with Δ²>1000 were excluded, without a count or inclusive aggregate.
tables.data_and_statistics: Refractory synthetic data with T=2000,3000,5000,7000 and Ñ=2050,2956,5222,6887. Exp, Gau, Ber, Bonnet, and Ours are compared on Δ² and CPU seconds. Means and SEs are shown; outlier exclusion is described in §4.1.2 rather than encoded as a row.
tables.evidence_relation: §4.1.2 and Table 2 provide the inhibitory-regime counterpart to Table 1; Appendix A Figure 2 shows the corresponding negative-kernel shapes. The nearby text and conclusion discuss post-hoc clipping, so the table supports robustness under the stated regime rather than unrestricted intensity validity.
design_strengths: Reusing Table 1’s paired columns makes the regime comparison direct.
T/Ñ and the same five method names preserve cross-table traceability.
The table sits next to the text that explains inhibitory kernels and the Ber outlier condition.
design_weaknesses: “Notations follow Table 1” prevents standalone interpretation of Δ², CPU, and the statistical rule.
Excluded outliers change the effective denominator, which cannot be recovered from the table.
The narrow layout compresses five method groups and still omits hardware, failure rate, and setup details.
tables.reusable_pattern: For a second data-generating regime, retain the main table’s column and statistical grammar, state inherited definitions explicitly, and expose any changed denominator or exclusions in the object.

tables.label: Table 3

caption.text: Table 3: Performance of Ours regarding the support window A on mutually-exciting scenario dataset (T = 5000) across 10 trials with standard errors in brackets.

tables.uncertainty: One mean row and one parenthesized standard-error row over 10 trials; no significance marking or interval is shown.
tables.data_and_statistics: Ours on mutually-exciting data with fixed T=5000 and support window A∈{1,2,5,10,20}. Δ² is 0.51, 0.24, 0.20, 0.29, 0.33; CPU seconds are 1.75, 3.89, 10.7, 22.5, 39.1. The tested grid puts the lowest Δ² at A=5, with no selection rule or budget column.
tables.evidence_relation: §4.1.3 defines A as a shape/compute hyperparameter; Table 3 is the sole main-text one-factor ablation. It links the Table 1 accuracy–cost axes to a support-window choice and does not decompose kernel, QMC, or Cholesky components.
design_strengths: The hyperparameter levels, error, and computational cost are aligned in adjacent pairs.
Fixed T and 10-trial SE give the ablation a clear experimental boundary.
A minimal black-and-white table makes the apparent A=5 tradeoff easy to scan.
design_weaknesses: Five tested values do not establish a selection or cross-validation rule.
No independent uncertainty comparison, budget, or significance assessment distinguishes the apparent optimum.
The two-row mean/SE format demands vertical alignment across a wide narrow table.
tables.reusable_pattern: For a single continuous hyperparameter, place quality and cost side by side across a fixed grid and retain a matched uncertainty row; add selection and budget metadata when making a tuning claim.

tables.label: Table 4

caption.text: Table 4: Results on financial dataset across 10 trials with standard errors in brackets. nll is the negative log-likelihood on test data. N is the data size per trial. cpu is the CPU time in seconds. The other notations follow Table 1.

tables.uncertainty: A mean row and parenthesized standard-error row summarize 10 randomly constructed sequence pairs. Bold follows the inherited comparison convention; no additional failure or interval column is present.
tables.data_and_statistics: Financial dataset with U=2 and N=3319 per sequence; 10 random train/test sequence pairs. nll is lower-is-better test negative log-likelihood and cpu is seconds. The point estimates are Exp 8086/38.2, Gau 2899/7.17, Ber 1487/13.3, Bonnet 1829/550, Ours 1721/3.4, with the corresponding SEs in parentheses.
tables.evidence_relation: §4.2 transfers the Table 1/2 quality–cost comparison to a single-stock financial dataset; Table 4 is the real-world evidence behind the conclusion’s comparable prediction and efficiency statement. It does not provide cross-stock or cross-day robustness.
design_strengths: The same method order and paired quality/cost grammar as Tables 1–2 makes transfer to real data easy to audit.
The caption defines nll, N, cpu, and 10-trial SE.
Keeping both nll and CPU visible prevents an efficiency win from being read as a predictive-accuracy win.
design_weaknesses: A single stock/day and 10 random pairs provide a narrow external-validity surface.
Caption inheritance leaves Δ²/other notation and comparison details outside the table.
Hardware, split identity, outlier handling, and broader failure information are absent; 11 leaves are dense in the inset.
tables.reusable_pattern: Retain the main synthetic table’s quality-plus-cost columns for real data, while stating metric direction, unit, randomization unit, and repetition count in the caption.

tables.label: Table 5

caption.text: Table 5: Average CPU time in seconds across 10 trials. Ñ denotes the average data size per trial.

tables.uncertainty: Only average CPU seconds across 10 trials are shown; there is no SE, SD, failure count, or accuracy companion column.
tables.data_and_statistics: Larger refractory data sizes with T=10000,15000 and Ñ=8248,12748. Bonnet CPU is 9250 and 26406 seconds; Ours is 19.1 and 29.5 seconds. The table varies data size and method pair but does not report predictive quality.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix H.1 extends the data-size axis from Tables 1–2; Table 5 is the compact runtime check placed beside the equivalent-kernel proof. It supports a larger-N cost claim, not accuracy stability.
design_strengths: The minimum columns retain T, average data size, and the two relevant runtimes.
The large quantity contrast is easy to scan in a centered inset.
The caption defines the average and Ñ without adding decorative structure.
design_weaknesses: No dispersion, accuracy, hardware, or failure field accompanies the large runtime values.
Two T levels cannot separate asymptotic behavior from implementation constants.
Precision presentation mixes 26406 with 19.1 without a stated reporting rule.
tables.reusable_pattern: For a larger-data cost extension, keep the control axis, effective data size, and candidate runtimes in a compact table, then pair it with quality and variation evidence elsewhere.

tables.label: Table 6

caption.text: Table 6: Average CPU time in seconds across 5 trials.

tables.uncertainty: Average CPU seconds across 5 trials; no SE, SD, failure count, or interval is reported.
tables.data_and_statistics: At U=3, Exp/Gau/Ber/Bonnet/Ours take 124/7.03/10.8/413/5.04 seconds; at U=15 they take 1369/300/254/8513/29.9 seconds. The table is a two-point all-method snapshot used before the Ours-only scaling curve.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix H.2 connects §2.4 dimensional complexity to Table 6’s cross-method U comparison, then to Table 7 and Figure 3. It supports runtime robustness at two dimensions and does not test an accuracy ablation.
design_strengths: Two U settings and five methods fit in a small direct comparison.
CPU units are stated in the caption and the U=3 values can be checked against the main refractory table.
Monochrome rules keep the cost snapshot printable.
design_weaknesses: Two U levels cannot identify a scaling slope or transition.
Five-trial averages have no displayed variation.
Scenario, hardware, and U definition are inherited from the surrounding Appendix H.2 prose.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a small all-method snapshot to anchor a later single-method scaling curve, retaining shared units and method order across both objects.

tables.label: Table 7

caption.text: Table 7: CPU time in seconds of Ours regarding the dimensionality U across 5 trials with standard errors in brackets.

tables.uncertainty: Six U columns each have a mean CPU row and parenthesized standard-error row over 5 trials.
tables.data_and_statistics: For Ours at U=10,50,100,200,300,500, mean CPU seconds are 0.68, 5.05, 26.9, 160, 478, 2010; SEs are 0.26, 0.82, 0.67, 1.91, 6.70, 15.5. The table preserves measured variation but has no baseline or fitted scaling parameter.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix H.2’s empty-interaction setup produces Table 7’s measured U grid; Figure 3 plots the same means and adds O(U³), while Table 6 supplies the all-method U=3/15 anchor. Together they operationalize the §2.4 complexity discussion.
design_strengths: The six U values match Figure 3 one-to-one.
Mean and SE rows preserve exact numeric evidence that the curve omits.
The compact repeated-column structure makes the runtime trend readable without color.
design_weaknesses: The six horizontal groups are small at inset width.
No theoretical reference value, slope estimate, hardware, or baseline series is included.
Only Ours appears, so cross-method dimensionality growth must be inferred from Table 6.
tables.reusable_pattern: Keep the raw means and trial variation in a companion table with exactly the same x grid as the plotted curve; reserve the chart for trend and reference geometry.

tables.label: Table 8

caption.text: Table 8: Estimation accuracy of triggering kernels and predictive performance by Ours. Results are on the mutually exciting scenario dataset, averaged over 10 trials, with standard errors in brackets. nll is the negative log-likelihood on the test data. Δ² denotes the integrated squared error for triggering kernel estimation, of which results are a reproduction of those presented in Table 1.

tables.uncertainty: Three T groups each have means and parenthesized standard errors over 10 trials. H.4 additionally says the prediction experiment was repeated 10 times; that nesting is not a separate table dimension.
tables.data_and_statistics: Ours on mutually-exciting data with training T=2000,3000,5000. nll means are 3294, 3013, 2842 and Δ² means are 0.38, 0.27, 0.20, with the corresponding SEs in parentheses. Training T changes data size at the same time as both metrics, so the three rows show an association rather than an identified causal effect of Δ² on nll.
tables.evidence_relation: Table 1 supplies the reproduced kernel-error values; Appendix H.4 places them beside test nll to examine the accuracy–prediction relationship. The table supports a compact downstream association check and reproduction trail, not a causal mediation or per-trial correlation analysis.
design_strengths: Adjacent nll and Δ² columns expose estimation and prediction together.
The caption defines both metrics, trial aggregation, SE, and the reproduction link to Table 1.
Three T groups are easy to cross-check against the main mutually-exciting table.
design_weaknesses: The different scales and directions of nll and Δ² are not marked in the table header.
Only three aggregated points are shown; paired trial-level relationships and correlation are unavailable.
The repeated prediction layer is described in H.4 prose rather than represented in the table.
tables.reusable_pattern: Place an intermediate estimator metric next to a downstream metric along the same training axis, and state the aggregation and reproduction source so a visual association is not mistaken for a causal mechanism.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: 理论 transformed-kernel estimator 与 §2.4 complexity 先在 Tables 1–2 中落到两种 synthetic regime 的 accuracy/runtime，再由 Table 3 的 A 消融、Table 4 的 financial 数据和 Appendix Figures 1–2 的 shape evidence 扩展；Appendix Tables 5–7/Figure 3 回收 N/U scaling，Table 8 检查 Δ² 与 nll 的并列关系。
cross_object_system.caption_system: 11 个对象均采用 “Figure/Table n:” 加描述句的 caption；Table 1、4、8 说明较多统计和缩写，Table 2 明确继承 Table 1，Figures 1–2 只定义 scenario/虚线真值，Figure 3 定义蓝/黑系列。caption 均为 regular，未直接写定量主发现。
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Tables 1–2 共享 T/Ñ → method → Δ²/cpu 两级表头；Table 3 将 A 置于上层，Table 4 使用 N → method → nll/cpu；Tables 5–8 以 T/U 为上层、metric/cpu 为下层。横线承载分组，避免完整竖线网格。
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Theorem 1/Propositions 2–4 的估计接口由 Tables 1–2 的主比较承接，Table 3 是 support-window 单因素消融，Table 4 是 real-world transfer；Tables 5–7/Figure 3 只扩展成本轴，Table 8 复现 Table 1 的 Δ² 并并列 nll。全文没有删除 kernel/QMC/Cholesky 等组件的独立消融。
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: 正文 Tables 1–4 在 §4.1–§4.2 形成主证据，文字明确调用 Appendix A Figures 1–2；附录 H.1/H.2/H.4 以 Tables 5–8 和 Figure 3 扩展数据量、维度、solver/grid 背景与 accuracy–prediction 关系。Table 7 与 Figure 3 共用 U 网格，Table 8 明确复现 Table 1。
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: 表格和 caption 的 Roman/Computer Modern 系统一致，Figure 1–2 的 Arial/AppleSymbols 与 Figure 3 的 mixed plot fonts 是局部例外；字号大多约 8.767–9.963 pt，图中小数学字形可降至约 1.691 pt。
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Figure 1–2 内部稳定复用五方法颜色，但表格依赖方法文字表头；Figure 3 重新定义蓝/黑为 measured/reference。没有跨表 color key，因此跨对象追踪主要依赖稳定的 method names。

most_reusable_patterns: Figures 1–2 的同构 3×3 facet、统一尺度、真值虚线和直接标签，适合矩阵函数的跨机制形状对照。
Tables 1–2/4 的 paired quality–cost columns，将误差或 nll 与 CPU 放在同一决策面，并在 caption 交代 trials/SE。
Table 7 + Figure 3 的原始均值/SE 表与 log–log 理论参考线配对，用表保留数值、用图展示复杂度趋势。
Table 3 和 Table 5 的小型单因素/规模扩展表面，围绕核心控制轴避免加入无关装饰。
highest_value_objects: Table 1：理论 estimator 的首个 synthetic accuracy–runtime 主比较。
Table 2 与 Figure 2：inhibitory regime 的 robustness、异常值边界和 kernel shape。
Figure 1：9-panel mutually-exciting shape evidence，与 Table 1 形成 quantitative/qualitative 对照。
Table 7 与 Figure 3：维度成本的精确数值、trial 变异和 O(U³) 视觉参照。
failure_patterns: 三幅 Figure 都缺少 trial identity/uncertainty display；Table 5–6 也只有均值，机制动态和不确定性覆盖不均。
Table 2 的 Ber outlier 排除只在正文叙述，排除数量与 inclusive sensitivity 无法从对象恢复。
Table 2/4 依赖 Table 1 notation，多个 caption 未定义 Δ²、U 或 scenario；Figure 2 裁剪后会失去共享图例。
Figure 1–2 五色曲线缺乏 marker/线型冗余，灰度或重叠区域中的方法识别成本较高；Figure 3 只有 Ours scaling。
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: 用黑白 paired accuracy–cost 表建立理论 estimator 的主证据，再用同构 kernel grids 和 log–log scaling 图补上 shape 与复杂度直觉，附录以小型消融和复现表扩展范围，但 trial 变异、异常值和机制动态大多留在对象之外。
